searchText: There needs to be a list of signature first bytes. In that list would include 0x19, 1,2,3, some RLP starters, etc. We just don't know where to put such a list, as Ethereum community doesn't have a good place for mutable lists. Right, in that case the EIPs which would propose any signature which could conflict would need a thorough security analysis. There should be no double usage of leading bytes between EIPs. The whole point is to avoid having to do that security analysis. Right, well as far as I know the 0x19 message scheme is very widely spread and the standard to sign messages (I don't know why EIP 191 is still in draft) - if that is the case, then 0x19-prefixed transactions should be rejected for this reason. I agree that 0x19 should be on the list. The only open question is where the list lives. I don't disagree with you that 0x19 should be on it. 😄 Great 🙂 I don't know what the right approach here is, I think step 1 is to figure out why EIP 191 is still in draft 🤔 - this is a generally accepted as "the" signing scheme for arbitrary messages such as logins... It is very bad for people to implement draft EIPs in production environments. There is a reason EIPs go through phases, and it is partly to ensure they get proper feedback and people looking at them. When people go and implement a production app based on a draft EIP there are two possible options: 1. The EIP cannot be changed because people already implement it. 2. The EIP does change and now you have a bunch of non-standard apps out there claiming to be compliant when they aren't. Both are bad situations for standardization, so people should not be building production software around draft EIPs. ERC20 has this exact problem. It didn't get proper review before everyone can off and implemented it which has resulted in years of pain for the community.
